bottom_line: Metoprolol CR/XL vs placebo lowered all-cause mortality (relative risk 0.66 [95% CI 0.53–0.81]).
implications: In this population (NYHA II–IV, ejection fraction ≤0.40) followed for a mean of 1 year, the trial’s numbers support that adding metoprolol CR/XL to baseline therapy was associated with lower all-cause mortality (relative risk 0.66 [95% CI 0.53–0.81]) and fewer sudden deaths (0.59 [0.45–0.78]) and deaths from worsening heart failure (0.51 [0.33–0.79]) versus placebo; these results do not establish efficacy/safety in NYHA class IV specifically because few such patients were included.

major_points.text: Double-blind randomised controlled trial in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, added to standard therapy.
major_points.quote: We enrolled 3991 patients with chronic heart failure in New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class II–IV and with ejection fraction of 0·40 or less, stabilised with optimum standard therapy, in a double-blind randomised controlled study.

major_points.text: Randomisation followed a 2-week single-blind placebo run-in period.
major_points.quote: Randomisation was preceded by a 2-week single-blind placebo run-in period.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, analysed by intention to treat.
major_points.quote: Our primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, analysed by intention to treat.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with metoprolol CR/XL than placebo with reported relative risk and confidence interval.
major_points.quote: mortality rates were 7·2% and 11·0% per patient-year of follow-up, respectively, with a relative risk of 0·66 (95% CI 0·53–0·81).

major_points.text: Sudden death and death from worsening heart failure were each reduced with metoprolol CR/XL.
major_points.quote: There were fewer sudden deaths in the metoprolol CR/XL group than in the placebo group (79 vs 132, 0·59 [0·45–0·78]; p=0·0002) and deaths from worsening heart failure (30 vs 58, 0·51 [0·33–0·79]; p=0·0023).

major_points.text: No patients were lost to follow-up.
major_points.quote: No patient was lost to follow-up (figure 1).

major_points.text: Permanent early discontinuation of study drug was similar between groups.
major_points.quote: Study drug was permanently stopped early in 13·9% of the metoprolol CR/XL group and in 15·3% of the placebo group (0·90 [0·77–1·06]).

criticisms.text: Few NYHA class IV patients were included; efficacy and safety in severe chronic heart failure remains to be assessed.
criticisms.quote: We included few patients in NYHA functional class IV. The efficacy and safety of b-blocker treatment in patients with severe chronic heart failure therefore remains to be assessed.

criticisms.text: Study was not powered for separate analysis of mortality in patients with mild heart failure.

criticisms.text: Study was not designed to assess mechanisms underlying sudden death in chronic heart failure.

criticisms.text: Study was not designed or powered for separate analysis of idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and did not include patients younger than 40 years.
